Well, the sidebar says I can post a personal story, so I'm doing it. Here's an example of how someone was truly kind to me. A stranger, no less.

About 7 years ago, myself and my boyfriend (now husband) had just moved into an apartment. We were very young and everything we had went towards rent and utilities - See, we were both coming from abusive places, so it was imperative that we keep the apartment.

Anyway.

At the time I did not have medical insurance. I went to the pharmacist to pick up my prescriptions. I needed them - I get blinding migraines that disallowed me from working if I didn't have the meds, and have some other medical problems. Without insurance, the prescriptions cost a lot of money. When told the price, I sighed and said something to the effect of "Yeah, ok, I'll have to charge it, yay for more debt."

The pharmacist went to fill my order. I went about my business. I came back to the pharmacy, and the pharmacist pulled me to the side. She told me that the woman behind me on line had paid for my prescriptions. All $160.00 of them. She had heard me talking.

I was stunned. The woman didn't want to be identified but the pharmacist pointed her out. She was a middle aged black woman. She didn't seem particularly well off, but one never knows. I approached her and began to cry as I thanked her for her kindness. She just smiled and said "I know what it's like to have hard times."

I promised to pay it forward.

Now I have a good job. Every year I go to the pharmacy and give $50 -100 to put towards paying for the prescriptions of someone who can't afford them. Last year it helped a young mother buying medicine for her baby, an elderly woman and a middle aged woman who apparently thought she was on camera for some tv show and started crying tears of joy when she found out the truth.

That stranger's actions changed my life forever. Up until then I'd never felt a kindness like that. I never saw good in the world. She changed that and I am so thankful for it.
